abstract: The highly variable environmental conditions that photosynthetic organism experience in nature require rapid and long-term acclimatory responses. Light and CO2 availability are tightly linked within the cell. When light intensity rises, CO2 fixation accelerates, causing intracellular CO2 to become limiting for photosynthesis. Nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) mechanisms prevent over excitation of the photosynthetic electron transport chain and consequent damage by reactive oxygen species. Energy dependent quenching (qE) is the fastest NPQ component and responds to thylakoid lumen acidification, a consequence of photosynthesis limiting CO2 concentrations. In vascular plants, the thylakoid K/H antiporter KEA3 is required for qE downregulation after a high to low light transition, transiently enhancing photosynthetic quantum yield. Here, we demonstrate that the same holds for the unicellular green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (Cr). Unlike vascular plants, CrKEA3 also contributes to qE relaxation in the dark and influences growth. The crkea3 mutants from higher light intensities, showed increased qE compared to the wild type (WT) background and grew more slowly. The growth reduction was accompanied by increased accumulation of low-CO2-induced (LCI) proteins, suggesting that crkea3 mutants experience a relative CO2 deficit. Our data suggest that KEA3 activity modulates multiple regulatory layers of photosynthesis in unicellular green algae, extending beyond the functions previously described for vascular plants.

metadata.title: The thylakoid K+ exchange antiporter KEA3 affects NPQ dynamics and growth in the green algae Chlamydomonas reinhardtii

summary: KEA3 antiporter in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii modulates qE relaxation, including in darkness, and affects growth and low-CO2-induced protein accumulation.
title: The thylakoid K+ exchange antiporter KEA3 affects NPQ dynamics and growth in the green algae Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
